Also just replayed "Il Cervo" Kaori event. I did not notice the first time because of the deep fried image, but at the end of the event it is Sekai talking through Kaori (red eyes). With that in mind and the context of the Gabriele D Annunzio poem "Il Cervo" and the previous dear parts story. the event starts to make a lot more sense.

View attachment 3615072

A rough outline of the last part of the event.(formatting might suck sorry)

-After Ami says she would like to bring the moon back Sekai starts talking through Kaori (and Ami is able to hear her).
-She then talks a bit about the nature of the world. (Im not sure yet what she means by "I have always been a dear". If she is referring to the themes of the poem or the previous dear parts story basically).
-Then she says "But together, we make the perfect nuclear family".(You could possibly take that as confirmation from Sekai of the Ami is Akira's daughter theory).
-"Together we are Il Cervo."(Referring to the poem probably. It would fit somewhat as a metaphor for Akira's current relationship with Sekai. The themes of the poem summarised are basically: hunter and dear, predator and prey, pursuit and desire, memory and melancholy, futility.)

Anyway make of that what you will. I'm still thinning about it in the context of the rest of the event. (Sorry if someone already posted this I kind of skim read the last 20 or so pages of the thread and might have missed it.)
Click to expand...
There's a lot last update that I'm kind of saving for later, but the Kaori "deer" stuff was in reference to Ami's story about having deer parts inside and being different than others.

"Il Cervo" also translates to "The Deer".

Basically, Ami's story seemed to be referring to how some people function differently than others, and those people are treated like they have something inhuman in them and that they need to be fixed by having it removed. Kaori and Ami have virtually always been different than others (same with Sekai and Sensei). Kaori also seems to have parts of others (possibly Sekai's organs) in her.

"Il Cervo" and what Kaori seemed to be saying is that they are all "deer". All of them are different, and all of them are prey, being stalked and admired by their hunter. (May also simply be saying they are all a singular deer as in parts of a whole) Together they are perfectly "normal" (nuclear).

"We are helpless and full of beauty" - The Deer/Il Cervo.

At least, that's my take at the moment.

posts.content_html_raw:
So I am playing catch up from years ago. I remember loving this game doing all the decoding by hand, all the freaking amazing lore, and just speculating on just about everything. I stopped around slightly after Yasu was introduced. I am reaching the point where I fell off before and I happen to recall and am experiencing again a severe lack of Maya, as she is my favorite and objectively best and most interesting character. I look at the new hints mod and see she still only has 20 scenes 12 of them I have reached at this point. I understand her underutilization due to her ties to the main plot and point being made that you are now supposed to get more info out of Noriko and Niki, but come on... Futaba has fucking 27 fucking events by comparison...

I reach out to my fellow Maya fans, will I be eating good soon, or should I brace for disappointment due to lack of content?

It's also really weird to me that there are 6 chapters but I am more than halfway through all the scenes. Are the locked chapters not done or are following chapters just filled a lot less? OR is it because I am sort of min maxing with hints and the game expected me to waste time? I guess I should also not the mod seems to only be up to date to the LAST patch, not the newest.

Fuck I missed this game. Its one of the few games I ever threw money at.

Yumi is like the only girl that Sensei has sacrificed a significant amount of time helping without receiving sex for it. The main reason initially was probably guilt due to assaulting her, but at this point, Sensei has pointed out that there's something valuable within the relationship as he himself is confused on what he wants the endgame to be.



She's also one of the girls that he truly feels comfortable with revealing how weak of a person he actually is to. Perhaps the fact that he doesn't feel the need to seduce her, and that she holds no real expectations for him, helps.



This ties in with several themes of the game. First is love - obviously if your goal from day one is to get in their pants that's kinda a perversion of what love means. Second is redemption - his chance to significantly improve the life of someone else. Just as he finds meaning in being a father for Ami and improving her life, perhaps there's also meaning in helping Yumi grow as a person outside of just exploiting her vulnerabilities for sex. It's like that story The Spider's Thread - just as the sinner was offered a chance to redeem himself from hell due to the one good thing he's done, Sensei might similarly view this as one of his last chances to become a good person.

The connection with Niki isn't really significant beyond the joke that they're both tsunderes.

But one thing to consider about Akira's relationship with Maya that I don't think has been discussed much, Is how much their relationship mirrors his own relationship with Sekai. That mirroring, the fact that he is the one that put her in that position, and what he seems to take from it is really extremely fucked up.
He cares about her more than the others because he can understand her more than them as she is in the same position he was in with Sekai. Additionally and quite tragically, Maya seems to have come to the same conclusion In thinking that they are the only people that can understand each other.
I think I'm not doing a good job of expressing what I'm thinking about them. But essentially Akira is to Maya, What Sekai was to Akira. In this context their relationship is really quite dark, if not the darkest in the game so far.
Edit: Specifically, him doing to her what Sekai did to him being a major factor enabling their relationship to progress to the point that loosing her would break him in the way loosing Sekai broke him is just super fucked up.

posts.content_html_raw:
BTW, it might seem sudden that I have become so invested in Yumi. It is somewhat sudden, isn't it? I didn't really like Yumi all that much before. She was a typical bully, which is not a type of character I particularly enjoy (to be honest, I also didn't particularly like Futaba, so I wasn't too concerned about Yumi bullying her, I was more concerned about the fact that it was bullying in general). She might even be a tsundere, which I don't usually like. But over time, I started to develop a warmer feeling towards her. Now, here we are - she is one of my favorite characters.

I think I started to like her more somewhere around... 0.32, maybe even earlier. But I just checked my old tier lists and Yumi was already higher than C at that point. I can't remember exactly what happened at that time and maybe I was playing events from older updates, as I only started playing LiL when 0.31 was released. Anyway, 0.32 was when I realized that I had started to like her more than simply "oh, another girl in the class".

Anyway, Yumi does grow up as a person: she tries to change herself and become a better person, just like Akira... and both of them failed at some point (Yumi beats up Nodoka and Akira gives up on being a good person after Maya Prime's "death"). Yumi gives her mom a second chance and finds a new friend, Noriko. Yumi and Akira also have some serious bonding moments, so they spend time together, slowly becoming friends... If we ignore the fact that Akira wants to have sex with her, their relationship is actually interesting.

And I think this is why it makes their kind of relations interesting. Yumi is not one of those girls who only like Akira because of his big penis. She doesn't understand if she loves him because all she knows is that Sensei makes her feel special, cared for in some way. For Yumi, who has been without a proper parent figure, Akira is the first person to show her some comfort... Alas, the true nature of their relations is more darker. He is lusting after her and she knows that.

And their relations kinda correlates with his relations with Io, actually. He supports her as well, caring about her and make feel special. He is lusting after her as well, but... Io is a bit naive about him, seeing only the best in him, just like Noriko, not gonna lie, but Noriko is somewhat crazy while Io just really wants to have someone to protect her, to be the parent figure she never had as well as Yumi. Yumi, on the other hand, is not as naive. She does see both light and dark in his figure. Both Io and Yumi have really shit-ass childhood, but Io was sexually abused by a parent (as someone theorized here) while Yumi was just totally neglected. That makes me ask why Io fells in love with a predator, but that's for another day.

You know, if Sensei wasn't a predator, it might be actually pretty cute story about delinquent slowly becoming invested into her teacher. In a perfect world, he'd have adopted her and/or would help her reunite with her mother.

And I kinda like that we start talking about Yumi way more often after the headcanon of mine, lmao.

When i was rereading some old events, i was thinking about what could differentiate the people we interact with the shadow people, you know, those in the background, that may or may not even real people to begin with. And then i thought about it how much some of the characters actually share some traits with akira. Like, guilt, abandonment issues, loss of a important person, self loathing, not been able to let go, not been a good person and all that.

I have often stated that i did believe this whole timeloop thing did feel like it was there to punish maya. But what if this isnt really so much about her and akira, but about everyone with a face? I mean especially the loss part and/or been abandonet is something a lot of characters share in one way or the other.

Chika and Chinami, abandonet by father iirc and lost the mother.
Yumi, abandonet by mother, neglected by father.
Ayane, neglected by father, i dont remember anything about her mother right now, not even if she was ever mentioned, so i will just assume she is out of the picture as well.
Sara and Sana, father left, lost bother/son.
Makoto, Maki lost father/husband, i mean he was already so long out of the picture even before his death and neglected by her mother that she started to project her need for a father figure on to him for a while already.
Miku, lost parents.
Futaba, i am not sure if she actually did qualify for the loss/abandonment in any way. At least i cant recal anything in that regard. Feel free to correct if there is something i just dont remember.
Rin, abandonet by both parents and got adopted.
Ami, lost both parents.
Maya, i think we can assume she lost both parents or got abandonet by them? Never clearly stated what, but something is clearly going on.
Molly, i mean she did left her home, family and friends, so i guess that counts? Maybe her mother is dead? At least i always just remember her talking about her father.
Tsuneyo, mother is dead i think, and her father is dying for a few million years by now, you know, how normal do these things.
Uta, she lost her grandfather, or at least i think that was uta.
Io, i dont remember if we ever got told it, but she is living with her aunt, so something must have happened even when i dont remember what.
Nodoka, i have actually no idea. Dont remember if that was ever brought up. But the fact how hard on she is for becomming his daughter has to count for something.
Otoha, i actually have no idea. I mean her parents are still there. But maybe the whole bother thing with him is hinting at something.
Touka, neglected by father.
Yasu, was adopted and after that i guess we can assume those new parents did abandon her as well.
Noriko, Niki, they both got abandoned by Akira.
Kirin, Karin, this is a hard one, because i cant think of anything that would qualify them her.
Haruka, her husband is gone for a while now.
Kaori, isnt it stated that her parents died in the accident? Yeah, think it is and then everyone believed her to be dead as well.
Yuki, did abandon her daugther and i guess she herself didnt really had contact to her family for whatever reason.
Wakana, Osako, i dont know, i mean Wakana did cut ties with her rich family, but beyond that i cant think of anything.
Tsukasa, neglected by the whole family as the backup daughter.
Imani, was there not something about some dead siblings? At least i remember that been implied to be connected to her burns.
Rika, got kicked out by her spouse.
Nao, got clearly abdandoned by her eldritch family. Probably because she was just too creepy even for them.

Edit for some corrections, note of thanks go to LoveBlueHairedGirl.

I guess I'm just gonna keep spewing my thoughts here throughout my current playthrough, but I'm currently fascinated by the dorm hallway patterns.
When Molly gets added, and with our expanded knowledge of Maya's backstory, it becomes really clear what is shared between Molly, Maya, and Yumi. Otoha I'm not so sure of but maybe it's the time she forcibly kissed Niki? I think there might be more to her being grouped with the consent coalition, since the other three are more about Akira acting on them, having Otoha be there for the Niki thing feels kinda out of place, though she does parallel Akira in some interesting ways. We shall see if something more comes of that.

So what about Wednesday? The girls are Chika, Rin, Noriko... and Tsuneyo? Chika Rin and Noriko are easy, obsessive adoration to a harmful degree. Also it might have some kind of fallout resulting from the relationship. Rin is obvious, Chika's foreshadowing beats you over the head with an iron pipe, and Noriko's has potentially already happened (the Ami thing. Honestly a pretty big deal, but even though she ghosts akira for a bit it didn't really feel that impactful to me honestly. She might have somthing bigger coming. Maybe Niki related?)
but then, what about Tsuneyo? Her being grouped with that trio is pretty interesting. Might imply something about her arc is headed, and it only makes me more curious about things to come. She does seem to have been more impacted by the husband roleplay than it first seemed, after all.

And Tuesday is a big case of Not Enough Information. Futaba, Miku, Io, and Touka. One of these things is not like the others. There are honestly several different things that could be tying Futaba, Miku, and Io together, and it comes down to what happens with Touka to be the deciding factor there. Though considering the gravity of the others, and how defining they are, I'm kinda worried about Touka. Also makes it seem like Futaba's issues might make a comeback.

okay, the time has come, first full replay - let's goooo


Everytime I see this intro sequence i keep wondering who this is, and trying to justify in my head why it's Himawari.

It seems to take place as Akira is either being thrown into the resets for the first time, or between resets. It also seems to state that he didn't die from his suicide, but is on the verge of death as well (maybe a coma).



One of the reasons I think it's Himawari is because this narrator seems to care for Akira, while also not knowing that much about him. That she loves him could also be just because he's her father, which wouldn't require that they know eachother well.

And there is this recurring theme with Himawari where she says things have an order to happen in order for everything to achieve a good ending (she snaps at Moyo about this as well), and here she says that all these conversations will make Akira hate her, but she has to have them because he needs to grow, and that's her job.


That they barely know eachother discards Maya, Ami, Sekai, and anyone else really. The following could point out at her being his child, any other god would know and have agency in meeting him, but his child would depend on her being born in the first place. Or be given leave by the gods to do so preemptively.



But then it starts to get confusing.



This directly contradicts what NAO says (not that her and Himawari agree in the first place). I don't remember Himawari's position on all of this being real or not, but it would still be in character with Himawari's policy of "keep smiling" though.



Himawari seems to be the one that believes in him in their every encounter. That they're a lot closer is being related.



What was on the rooftop? Maya and maybe Ami watching from afar. His trauma with Sekai. But she wants him to become a better him, which would also fall into what Himawari believes, that all the suffering leads to a better outcome. HOPE says the direct opposite, Pareidolia doesn't seem interested in him growing either, Wires is whatever, and NAO says it doesn't matter.

Keep smiling.

After going over what exactly the girls have lost, it seems that Otoha may be the only main girl that doesn't have some understanding of abandonment. Her parents are strict, but that's it.

As for the rest:
Ami - watched her parents die, and her uncle, as he himself has put it, has basically been a ghost ever since. May have also lost her grandmother before all of this.

Ayane - mother ditched her, and her father seems to not even look at her.

Chika (and Chinami) - father abandoned them, and mother died.

Futaba - parents are alive, but seemed to leave her behind to go traveling for a lot of her life, and just send her money.

Io - mother seems to have abused her, and she only lives with her aunt so her father is either not in the picture, or doesn't want to be.

Kirin - hasn't lost anyone, but at least seems to feel neglected by her parents, who seem to have given up trying to discipline her and just let her do whatever.

Makoto - mother seems to have never acted like a mother until recently, and her father has apparently been gone since leaving for the space war a few years ago.

Maya - had nowhere else to go before meeting Sensei, and tends to be referred to as a "stray cat". Family doesn't seem to be in the picture, and there doesn't seem to be any way to contact them.

Miku - parents were murdered in front of her.

Molly - mother killed herself.

Nodoka - father is never mentioned (besides maybe with the "she has my eyes" bit recently), and it doesn't seem like her mother is all there, considering Nodoka is constantly checking up on and taking care of her, including being implied to having to bathe her, and maybe having to work since she was 10 at least.

Noriko - big brother figure/crush/tutor ditched her. Niki also probably wasn't all there for a while considering she was depressed and suicidal. Seems to have cared about Ami and Maya, before they also disappeared. Less so in Ami's case, I assume.

Rin - bio parents abandoned her to an orphanage.

Sana - brother was murdered, father abandoned her, mother seems to try to pretend her brother never existed to cope.

Touka - father doesn't seem to give his family much attention. Touka's also been abandoned by past tutors, and never was able to make any friends.

Tsuneyo - mother is not in the picture, and she doesn't seem to look like her father, while being extremely grateful to him, so she may have been adopted. Recently, her father has become sick and she has to run their business.

Uta - brother went to prison for apparently trying to kill her stalker, and after her family sent her away, her grandpa seemed to die in front of her leaving her all alone in Kumon-Mi, besides Io.

Yasu - parents seemed scared of her, mother considered her a monster, and they are no longer in the picture. Doesn't seem to recall what it is like to have a mother or a home.

Yumi - mother ditched her, but she also seemed to have lost her cousin Kaori and her aunt and uncle, due to the accident that happened to Kaori. (Her dude friends also seemed to disappear thanks to the space war.)

My thoughts on Io and Nodoka after you know:

Io might be a little psycho:
Io - "Sometimes, I think about murdering people for reasons that don't even pertain to you. So probably."
But, she'd probably consider doing anything to Nodoka after what happened as "Nodoka winning", so it's doubtful anything will come from it, besides more medication.

Yumi tried to kill Nodoka, and Nodoka laughed about it:
Nodoka - "Heheheheh..."
- "It was worth every last punch..."
- "If getting hit like that...allows me to be the meat of a lesbian sandwich...I should get into fights more often..."
So, it's not like hurting Nodoka accomplishes anything.

Nodoka also seemed to note that what she was about to do to Io was pointless unless something comes from it, right before doing it:
Nodoka - "For example, simply spilling out traumatic events from a character's past would serve no purpose other than to-"
Simply attacking Nodoka would at the least be something she'd expect, like she did with Uta:
Nodoka - "I take it you are going to hit me now?"

If I were to guess, Nodoka is probably trying to change Io like she changed Yumi. If so, she's likely already achieved her goal, since Io reacted and it's changed people's view on her, but we'll see.

Might lead to Io becoming friendlier like Yumi somewhat has, though. Or maybe getting involved in the resets as Yumi only did, after trying to talk to Sensei about what happened. Albeit, the timeskip stuff may have just been random and Yumi was "lucky".

posts.content_html_raw:
Antosha said:
Sure. All the characters are doing their best, even when their best is actually not that great — that’s good writing.

But Nodoka’s “higher purpose” is no excuse for being needlessly cruel. At least with Yumi I can see what she’s reacting to. Kirin is just a walking ball of libido, and does some things that are beyond not okay — but she doesn’t do them just because she can. She does them because she desperately wants to get laid. Ami is batshit — and I think Sensei is only partially responsible. Io isn’t great with people (other than Uta and Sensei, for some reason). All the other characters do things that hurt others. But they do so while trying to achieve goals that we can understand. Sort of. (Love ya, Yasu!)

Nodoka, though? I get her dedication to her “art,” I really do, and the in-game logic of her trying to do… whatever the fuck it is she’s trying to do.

But as you say, it doesn’t make any of it acceptable.

If it turns out she’s a direct conduit to one of the “gods” like Yasu, Kaori, and Tsuneyo seem to be, I’ll at least feel as if there’s some excuse. But acceptable? Nope.
Click to expand...
Well, she barely treats the characters as people but rather "characters" for her story. But I think the Nodokathon thing explains her perspective pretty well.

It's impossible for her to fully understand everything in the world, therefore she wants to delude herself into seeing a world where she can understand anything, and hopefully that world manifests itself into reality. Similar conceptually from the main gimmick in Chaos;Head, if you've played that.

Now, this is my speculation, but Sensei's story in a way affirms the way she sees the world. And her writing this story is her teaching others that this is how the world works, getting her closer towards the goal mentioned above.

Why she feels such a need to create this world, we're not really sure? Perhaps there's something she can't understand - she has her theory, and affirmation that indeed the world is this way will give her the answer? Or maybe she's just autistic. Who knows.

Moonflare said:
I liked the Nodokathon, but Selebus messed up. That it happened after the shit she pulled with Io made absolutely no narrative sense. Like, I only enjoyed it on my second viewing cause the first time I was like "how are these girls even here after that?".
Click to expand...
Yeah. I get what you're all saying, absolutely. When the Nodokathon started, I had to walk away for a couple of days. It really wasn't something I was in the mood for at all when it first happened -- and I couldn't imagine most of the girls going along with it after what Nodoka did to Io. Noriko especially, but most of the others seem as if the last thing they'd have wanted to do was be anywhere near Nodoka, let alone agree to play one of her... games.

When I came back to it, it still bothered me, but the fan-service-ness of it, as if Sel were saying, Geeze, you pervs, you want these girls to have sexy times? Here you go! actually made it funny to the point of being more palatable. I could enjoy the ridiculousness of the whole thing. And Sana finally showing the other girls her inner freak really was wonderful. (I'll be shocked if Rin and Kirin don't hook up at some point -- probably with Akira along for the, um, ride.)

Moonflare said:
Man, I feel for Yasu so much. Someone commented the other day about how they didn't like her, and I missed out on replying. But she's so close to some real life situations, where the person is a shell of themselves and throw themselves completely into a specific belief in order to survive - and specifically her last event (the doctor appointment ones) broke me.
Click to expand...
Absolutely. That was actually too painful for me do in AVN form. I had to open the script and just read the text -- which was brutal enough. It was hard enough to think of her as a conduit to a crazy-ass deity. Good for occasional comedy, occasionally creepy as hell. But that?

A bunch of the characters make me feel this way -- even Akira. As someone else said, the only main characters who haven't dealt with some major mind-fuckery are Otoha and Touka. And I'm guessing, based on what we've seen so far, that that's just because we don't know about it. (Nodoka may not have, but she's already batshit insane. Not sure that Futaba had struggled with anything worse than body image issues, which are bad enough... but then Nodoka moved in. And Karin has now weathered Hurricane Sensei.)

Honestly? What about half of the cast needs more than anything is serious, professional clinical help. The girls are dealing with loss/abandonment, sexual assault (not all of it from Sensei), and various forms of PTSD. None of the adult women (excepting maybe Tsubasa) is exactly sane -- with reason. And some of the characters... Ami? Yasu? Miku? Io? Sensei? These people are not capable of caring for themselves. I'm not going to say that psychiatry offers any kind of guarantee, but aside from Io's overflowing pharmacopeia, we don't see any sign that any of the grieving, fucked up women (and one man) are getting any help at all.

Which, I don't know, may be the point? I mean, this is a horror AVN. And what's scarier than a broken mind?

An Interesting thing that I don't think was ever brought up about the 'Mother May I' Chapter 3 Main Event; Nodoka seemed to notice Sensei's sudden change:
View attachment 3622374 View attachment 3622376 View attachment 3622378 View attachment 3622379 View attachment 3622381 Ami - "And I love so, so much." (Nodoka smirking)
Young Sensei - "Ugh...what am I going to do with you?"
Sensei - "Ami wins." (Nodoka being the only one looking at him, and no longer smirking)
Ami - "Huh?..."
Nodoka - "..."
Watch her natural smirk disappear.
Click to expand...
I mean, given that she knows what she knows - could be less supernatural and just that she understands why Ami won. Or maybe she realised just then (and the whole Sekai, Akira being the Boy, this fucking blanket, and Ami's relationship with him clicked).

There's a thing I've been feeling about these girls as I think about them, that there are characters I like, and then there are characters it doesn't matter if I like them or not, but that should be valued because they have enormous potential to actually help Akira with the supernatural stuff. And Nodoka is slowly climbing up there.
Has Nodoka been a thing in previous resets? Cause she is mentioned many times in chapter 1, but so is Molly and other people.

But my question comes from the impression that Sekai has not being a thing in previous resets (amiokay's many punishments and deaths seem to attest to that because she seems to reference a past where she was together with Akira, and now there she is being killed on giant Ts, while babbling about what's buried beneath his feet, as HOPE states that he could even bring a Sekai that Akira could inseminate - which may be the intention with Kaori), and given that Nodoka has a profound interest in that part of the Arakawa's family, I just wonder if that is also the first time she's investigating this (maybe even the first time she wrote this book?).

(Being able to recall his past also seems to be something particular to this cycle, and NAO even mocks this, as if that would make difference - and it most certainly does. Which adds a layer to what Himawari says about Niki not even seeming real, indeed, she could just be yet another trigger particular to this cycle that intends to help him with remembering his past)

My point is, perhaps even Nodoka's whole thing about breaking the world is yet another attempt from Himawari, Wires, Pareidolia, or Sekai to change things in this particular cycle and make it different from all the others? Because mysterious narrator says that there are multiple worlds out there, and in most of them indeed nothing changes or nothing is real (can't recall the exact wording). But that this one could turn out different.

somepersonoutofnowhere said:
Honesty, I don't have a single clue on how she could've noticed in like, under half a second to everyone but the entire memory to Sensei making it longer, and Nodoka somehow noticing (maybe something else than noticing) during that.
Click to expand...
Nodoka seems very observant, so even something like Sensei's eyes glazing over would have probably been enough for her to get an idea that his mind went somewhere.

She later seems to be considerate enough to save something about Ami, that she thinks will affect Sensei, for when she thinks he can handle it:
Nodoka - "I know many things, Akira. But none of them particularly matter to me. And I'd be happy to tell you why I've been following your adorable niece around, but..."
- "Perhaps another day, when I think you're capable of taking a bigger hit, I'll share it with you."
So, she at least thinks she's got a grasp on Sensei's mentality.

The future Nodoka Ami plot is something I'm definitely looking forward to. She seems to be waiting for Ami to return to school and for Sensei to return to "normal", then she'll probably continue stalking Ami:
Ami - "What's your game, Nagasawa? Why do you keep following me around? And why are you suggesting competitions that will do nothing but make my flaws more visible?"
- "She's been following me around ever since the poetry thing, Sensei! It's starting to creep me out!"

Nodoka - "You see, Ami Arakawa is special. But not everyone realizes that just yet."
- "Ami Arakawa is the daughter of The Girl Who Cannot Breathe."
- "Frankly, I'm an idiot for not piecing it together sooner. I have no idea how it slipped by me so easily. But now that I'm actually thinking about it, everything fits. It all fucking fits.

Moonflare said:
I mean, given that she knows what she knows - could be less supernatural and just that she understands why Ami won. Or maybe she realised just then (and the whole Sekai, Akira being the Boy, this fucking blanket, and Ami's relationship with him clicked).

There's a thing I've been feeling about these girls as I think about them, that there are characters I like, and then there are characters it doesn't matter if I like them or not, but that should be valued because they have enormous potential to actually help Akira with the supernatural stuff. And Nodoka is slowly climbing up there.
Has Nodoka been a thing in previous resets? Cause she is mentioned many times in chapter 1, but so is Molly and other people.

But my question comes from the impression that Sekai has not being a thing in previous resets (amiokay's many punishments and deaths seem to attest to that because she seems to reference a past where she was together with Akira, and now there she is being killed on giant Ts, while babbling about what's buried beneath his feet, as HOPE states that he could even bring a Sekai that Akira could inseminate - which may be the intention with Kaori), and given that Nodoka has a profound interest in that part of the Arakawa's family, I just wonder if that is also the first time she's investigating this (maybe even the first time she wrote this book?).

(Being able to recall his past also seems to be something particular to this cycle, and NAO even mocks this, as if that would make difference - and it most certainly does. Which adds a layer to what Himawari says about Niki not even seeming real, indeed, she could just be yet another trigger particular to this cycle that intends to help him with remembering his past)

My point is, perhaps even Nodoka's whole thing about breaking the world is yet another attempt from Himawari, Wires, Pareidolia, or Sekai to change things in this particular cycle and make it different from all the others? Because mysterious narrator says that there are multiple worlds out there, and in most of them indeed nothing changes or nothing is real (can't recall the exact wording). But that this one could turn out different.
Click to expand...
Nodoka was probably around since she hung around Futaba, but like quite a few of the girls, she was going to the school that got swallowed at the beginning of Chapter 2, which is definitely something that hadn't happened before from Maya Prime's point of view.

If that never happened, Nodoka, Noriko, and Touka, etc, all wouldn't be in Sensei's class. Neither would Yasu. So, it's likely something supernatural was involved in that, and them being where they are, now. Something seemed to want the Nakayamas and Tsukiokas around Sensei.

Yasu also seems to be getting interferences and manipulated by something other than HOPE:

Yasu - "Because it not He who gives me these things. These thoughts..."
- "It is an interference."

Frankly, Pareidolia sucks, but this "the world itself" seems to be the thing to watch out for. It may be manipulating Yasu, Makoto, and Nodoka at least:
Yasu - "This is not His word, but the word of the world itself."
Makoto - "It's like the world itself is speaking to me."
Nodoka - "Through me, you can be forgiven. And all of your misdeeds or sins will be forgotten in the eyes of whichever god you follow, for I have been ordained by the world itself."

"The world itself" also does not seem nice:
Yasu - "Its tone is one of excitement...like it is anticipating what will soon befall us."
- "The world is not who will burn. It is all of us who live inside of it that will."

World also translates to Sekai, btw. So, the main Sekai roaming around, may be this thing, and Sekai seemed to imply she was up to something, back in Chapter 2:
Sekai - "I have to go now. I have things to do."

There's also how Maya Prime was apparently experiencing, right from the start, Upside Down dreams:
Maya - "I keep having these...strange dreams lately. And it's as if they're getting even stranger as the days go by."
- "They're hard to describe. It's like reality but..."
- "Upside down?"
Which were apparently strange to her, implying they were different than usual, and would imply something has been altering this timeline since the start.

Overall, some main notable differences in Chapter 1 before the school was swallowed, seem to be:
  • Yumi stopped Sensei from erasing himself in static.
  • Ami was convinced to become a Maid.
  • Maya was given that green scarf.
Sekai's shadow showed up in the event that led Ami to becoming a maid:
Ami - "Yup! I'm a mind reader. And right now, you're thinking that you want to take me shopping."
(Ami's Chapter 1 'Cute Girls and Stuff' Event. Which led to her next Event 'Divergence')

And The Shapeshifter/Himawari was the one who sold Sensei the scarves:
Non Chika Employee - "If you act now, I'll let you have both for just 4,000 Yen. My regional manager is on the way here anyway so I was actually just about to take them down and hide them."

Non Chika Employee/Shapeshifter/Himawari - "If you act now, I'll let you have both for just 4,000 Yen. My regional manager is on the way here anyway so I was actually just about to take them down and hide them."

Maya - "I really do..."
- "Have the worst luck in the world..."
Sensei Narrator - "I was being followed by a stray cat."
(Chapter 1 'Stray Cat' Main Event, and Chika's Chapter 3 'Rough Cuts' Event, revealed the Shapeshifter's involvement.)

These events also took place at the Mall which seems to be Pareidolia's territory based off the 'Amy' Happy Event mentioning the Pareidolia Mall, and the Mall suddenly being renovated in Spring/Currently.

Something has definitely been manipulating things in the background.

I wonder if Selebus planned for one of the characters of that game to be Akira's mom from the start, cause if so it is very bizarre that she'd show up at his laptop when he's traumatized by his mom, and looks to Sekai as an alternate mother figure instead. Click to expand...
Considering Sensei in the first Reset apparently meets and talks to Saki from his 'Nothing is Beautiful' game, in the 'Everything is Connected' Happy Event, which if missed is called 'Nothing is Beautiful':
https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=Everything_is_Connected
Which was long before Saki was revealed to be the name of his mother, I'd think it was planned.

Lessons in Love seemed to be intended to be a sequel to it. Of course, I could be wrong and it was just decided afterwards.

Nodoka's mom may show up in the remake, but that game only had a demo, and so far the only character from it that hasn't shown up in LiL (besides Josh?), is dark haired green eyed Reina:
Yuu Narrator - "This is Reina. She's probably the most ordinary person I know."
She's kind of like Sana, Karin, and Maya all put together, based off what little was shown of her.

Miu, and Yuu, both showed up in the recent 'Rain King' Happy Event, along with Saki, Kanon, and Tsurumi:
Tsurumi - "Wow! Look at this place, Kanon! It's tiny, but it's way nicer than the sewer! And super clean too!"
Tsurumi also recently showed up looking not good in Nao-chan's Chapter 4 'What's in the Pot?' Event:

Tsurumi - "I...I...I-I-I...I-I'm T-T-T...T-Tsurumi! And...A-And you're w-w...w-watching...W...What's in the Pot?!"

On the signs behind her - "TALK OR DIE" and "WHAT'S IN THE POT?"
Some Info on Kanon and Tsurumi from Sel's side game that never came to fruition called 'Grow Old. Then Die':
Tsurumi: A happy-go lucky, curious girl who is more independent than she has any right to be. Persuasive under the right circumstances and easily influenced. Will open up to just about anyone as long as she likes them.

Sister (Nameable) [is called Kanon in LiL]: Your twin sister. The first thing you saw when you were born. You have watched her live through Hell time and time again. You have watched how it changed her. She loves you very much. Do you love her?

The Demo of Sel's previous game 'Nothing is Beautiful' can be found on his Itch, btw, if anyone wants to play it and see where things may have started.

No, I'm not calling linear storytelling lame, in actual fact I'd much rather prefer if this was all linear, because his optional routes suck. For a story of this complexity to have branching paths is just too much, and he's nowhere near the level of design necessary to pull this off. He's a very good writer, but his design is, well, bad.

This is a good opportunity to mention that the beginning of the game has inconsistencies depending on which order you play things, and even when they don't, they simply flow better in a narrative sense if played in the order they appear on the menu. Not to mention that some things are just ridiculous, like not entering Chika's bedroom anymore until the beach trip cause otherwise you trigger the bad homie thing. How would you know this without a guide? It's like, why boggle down your story (which is the selling point) with this crap?

More to the point, his optional stuff feels like "I have this story that I want to tell, but I'll let you feel like you have some control and punish reward you by letting you miss parts of the story I want to tell" - cause that's all there is to it, you don't get new optional events, you get a red crossed title over the actual events that he wrote, and a poor attempt through dialogue changes to make the overall story still make sense despite what you missed.
I have seen the event variation, which is a Nodoka event (thought it was a Yumi one) called Matador. And it sucks. It's nowhere near as powerful and demeaning as the real one, to the point where this one feels fake.

How does "you were trying to fuck someone else other than Chika", compare to "you stood there while I was sexually assaulted and did nothing"? Lame doesn't cover it.

No, I'm not calling linear storytelling lame, in actual fact I'd much rather prefer if this was all linear, because his optional routes suck. For a story of this complexity to have branching paths is just too much, and he's nowhere near the level of design necessary to pull this off. He's a very good writer, but his design is, well, bad.
Spoiler:
general misgivings
This is a good opportunity to mention that the beginning of the game has inconsistencies depending on which order you play things, and even when they don't, they simply flow better in a narrative sense if played in the order they appear on the menu. Not to mention that some things are just ridiculous, like not entering Chika's bedroom anymore until the beach trip cause otherwise you trigger the bad homie thing. How would you know this without a guide? It's like, why boggle down your story (which is the selling point) with this crap?
More to the point, his optional stuff feels like "I have this story that I want to tell, but I'll let you feel like you have some control and
punish
reward you by letting you miss parts of the story I want to tell" - cause that's all there is to it, you don't get new optional events, you get a
red crossed title
over the actual events that he wrote, and a poor attempt through dialogue changes to make the overall story still make sense despite what you missed.
Spoiler:
Yumi and Nodoka stuff
I have seen the event variation, which is a Nodoka event (thought it was a Yumi one) called Matador. And it sucks. It's nowhere near as powerful and demeaning as the real one, to the point where this one feels fake.
Yumi feels bothered by Akira because he keeps looking at her naked (???), like, understandable, but you are naked, hot as fuck, both of you like one another, and he tries super hard not to look and offers you his shirt. Then she's also bothered because he was there to fuck someone that isn't Chika, and I'm like... seriously Yumi? This is dumb. She doesn't get his shirt, and would rather step out naked and find a flag or something to make it home. And Nodoka the all powerful evil bitch, just stays there like "wow, I guess Yumi's even more badass than me, and I won't follow through my blackmail cause if I ever was it would trouble you Akira" - like, what is this fanfic compared to the emotional trauma of what happened in the real event.
How does an attempt at blackmail that was foiled, compare to the terror that was sexual assault and cuckholding - leading to smashing Nodoka's face in? How does "you were trying to fuck someone else other than Chika", compare to "you stood there while I was sexually assaulted and did nothing"? Lame doesn't cover it.
Anyway seeing this just cemented my belief that there is one true way to play this game, which is by playing the story Selebus wants to tell (the one with all the events). And he should probably just tell that one instead of wasting time with this crap. Cause even thematically, let's face it, Akira never had a choice and if this is ours I'd rather not have it either.

The lounge chair creaked as I leaned a little further back than it wanted me to. I don't know why this is the only one we have when there are five of us here, but it is what it is.

I turn the page of my book, hoping for whatever weird collection of poetry I decided to pick up today to make any sort of sense to me, but if today is anything like the last (Which it will be), I doubt that will happen. [REDACTED] walks into the room and the scent of garlic drifts off of her lavender hair and over to me. Now, I know what you're thinking. Garlic isn't really the most "romantic" of smells out there. But, strangely enough, it makes me appreciate her more. In fact, pretty much everything makes me appreciate her more.

The position she leaves her shampoo bottle in, label facing the wall. How long she takes to get ready in the morning despite never having anywhere to go. The way the light reflects off her glasses. The way she says my name. Kyoko. Kyoko. With elongated o's not because she has trouble saying it, but because it's like she doesn't want the word to end. God I want to fucking mess her up right now.

--
A seemingly normal day in the upside down house.

Isn't Kyoko Nodoka's mom? Also, Sensei in Beyond the Reach of God suggests he knows this girl Kyoko is obsessed with:


"I also can’t say that I have any idea how to deal with this. So, at the risk of Nodoka actually digging until there is no skin left on her fingers, I should probably call on someone for help."
"Someone who may or may not have experience dealing with this girl in her manic state. And someone not named Otoha since she normally just bails."

"Thankfully, I know someone just like that. And it’s someone I should have invited along from the get go."
"And while she may not have lavender hair, the perfume she wears will compensate for it."

The lounge chair creaked as I leaned a little further back than it wanted me to. I don't know why this is the only one we have when there are five of us here, but it is what it is.
I turn the page of my book, hoping for whatever weird collection of poetry I decided to pick up today to make any sort of sense to me, but if today is anything like the last (Which it will be), I doubt that will happen. [REDACTED] walks into the room and the scent of garlic drifts off of her lavender hair and over to me. Now, I know what you're thinking. Garlic isn't really the most "romantic" of smells out there. But, strangely enough, it makes me appreciate her more. In fact, pretty much everything makes me appreciate her more.
The position she leaves her shampoo bottle in, label facing the wall. How long she takes to get ready in the morning despite never having anywhere to go. The way the light reflects off her glasses. The way she says my name. Kyoko. Kyoko. With elongated o's not because she has trouble saying it, but because it's like she doesn't want the word to end. God I want to fucking mess her up right now.
--
A seemingly normal day in the upside down house.

Interesting stuff regarding the upside down house, and it may add to that theory about Futaba reminding Akira of Nodoka's parents or something. There's this event where Futaba is supposed to show you what she wrote, but instead there's stuff written on the middle of the notebook by someone else, and here is what it says:



Now, Yumi said that if she were to have the perfect life it would be to stay up late, eat as much as she wants and live forever, I don't know if that's related to this (probably not) but there you go.


Now, given that the people that live in the upside down house are probably Nodoka's parents, that she is a stellar writer, and that Futaba often goes to sleep at her place, that this notebook is hers would be the logical conclusion. But I have no idea, cause Nodoka, at this point in time, doesn't seem to have any reason to fuck with Futaba (it's before the first reset). Thoughts?

Also, the edge of the universe seems to be the room with the clocks (could it be also the bottom of the well? I have no idea yet). And when Sana asks Akira if there is anywhere he'd like to go, he says the edge of the universe, which leads him to meeting Yasu for the first time.

You made sense, the issue is that it's a LOT. And I don't mean from you, but from the game and in fragments way too far apart. We'll eventually get it though. United we stand.

I've found a mention to a creaking seventh step recently (I thought it had to do with stairs, but maybe it's the floorboards?). But it could also just be nothing. The attic is mentioned plenty of times, including Ami at the beginning of the game. On your first weekend she says she's cleaning the house, and you should probably get on with your day outside then, cause she hasn't started with the attic yet and who knows how long that will take.

Akira also had a box with fragments of glass from the accident, and mentions that the box just disappeared. Could be with Maya, on that attic, or even on that mysterious grandma's house (which would be theirs now by all rights).

As a side-note, I just moved past the first reset and this first part of the game is heavily about Sekai at every turn. I'm starting to wonder about her actually, and if the girl that could not breathe was also a victim to someone. Nozomu (brother) seems sketchy at best. And the thing about the god creating other people just so he could fuck something, and then demanding that people don't fuck eachother, but people ignoring him - feels a little too close to Sekai and Akira fucking (and him knowing about it and being pissed, which has been implied a bit).

The way this is important and related to the house is because Saki is both their mom, and Nozomu is older - so what the hell even happened there. Yuu is never even mentioned in relation to the brothers, and just what made Saki hate Akira (or give up on him entirely). And just how did Sekai have to do with his parent's house anyway? When did they die, how does Ami even remember a grandma? so many questions...

(could also be Sekai's mom's house I suppose, but that would raise even more questions - while it would certain explain why she couldn't breathe having to always listen to papa).

spoilers.title: random things
spoilers.html:
I've found a mention to a creaking seventh step recently (I thought it had to do with stairs, but maybe it's the floorboards?). But it could also just be nothing. The attic is mentioned plenty of times, including Ami at the beginning of the game. On your first weekend she says she's cleaning the house, and you should probably get on with your day outside then, cause she hasn't started with the attic yet and who knows how long that will take.

Akira also had a box with fragments of glass from the accident, and mentions that the box just disappeared. Could be with Maya, on that attic, or even on that mysterious grandma's house (which would be theirs now by all rights).

As a side-note, I just moved past the first reset and this first part of the game is heavily about Sekai at every turn. I'm starting to wonder about her actually, and if the girl that could not breathe was also a victim to someone. Nozomu (brother) seems sketchy at best. And the thing about the god creating other people just so he could fuck something, and then demanding that people don't fuck eachother, but people ignoring him - feels a little too close to Sekai and Akira fucking (and him knowing about it and being pissed, which has been implied a bit).

The way this is important and related to the house is because Saki is both their mom, and Nozomu is older - so what the hell even happened there. Yuu is never even mentioned in relation to the brothers, and just what made Saki hate Akira (or give up on him entirely). And just how did Sekai have to do with his parent's house anyway? When did they die, how does Ami even remember a grandma? so many questions...

(could also be Sekai's mom's house I suppose, but that would raise even more questions - while it would certain explain why she couldn't breathe having to always listen to papa).

Click to expand...
Let's say we believe Maya Prime is, more or less, a normal girl that had normal parents, and her knowledge comes only from being stranded in a thousand resets.

We can assume that for as long as she's been awake, she's the one doing the resets through praying on the roof (how did she figure that out the first time is anyone's guess).

But then, she seems to tell every new fake sensei to carry boxes with her when the reset is close, she takes them from her dormroom to a specific room in the school, and no sensei is able to either look inside the boxes nor go into the room.

she makes no mention of the boxes when she says that anyone could make the reset. so it's probably not something that relates either to her survival nor the mechanics of the reset.

the gods don't seem to care about resets at all, so it's unlikely it's something against them. And since the last reset, we also know that ritual or no ritual, memories are preserved and the reset can be done easily (big boi does it no problem). so whatever is inside the boxes probably has to do with Akira himself.

We know the boxes don't protect Akira since he wanders through the town every reset. It doesnt prevent freaking HOPE from appearing inside the school either, so it's not even protecting the place. so maybe it's to prevent Akira himself from going into a specific place during a reset?

Now things get murky, where in school would be dangerous for Akira to go into during a reset? the only place I could think of is the room with the clocks. I mean, it fits right?

There's a room in school he can't bring himself to enter, and we never figured where the room with the clocks is. He jumped to death on the roof, from there we can assume he fell into the wishing well, and the room with the clocks is at the bottom of the wishing well. the room with the clocks is at the edge of the universe, but it would be the end of the universe if he wasn't stubborn - and the school is the edge/end of the world during a reset.

Hell, if we want to go wild we could say there are clocks inside the boxes. We know they're heavy - I just don't know if Ayane would have reacted with "I don't know sensei, this might" if she saw clocks inside. Probably not.

Regardless, maybe Akira can enter the room with the clocks during a reset, and Maya tries to prevent that, because it would bring about the end of the cycles I don't know.

If we instead assume Maya is a dream-child, then a lot changes - because she could have simply been taught how to reset the world, and a number of things that she didn't told us. Including but no limited to being the child of Akira/HOPE - but then things start to become way too crazy and without sufficient basis.

He jumped to death on the roof, from there we can assume he fell into the wishing well, and the room with the clocks is at the bottom of the wishing well. the room with the clocks is at the edge of the universe, but it would be the end of the universe if he wasn't stubborn - and the school is the edge/end of the world during a reset.
Hell, if we want to go wild we could say there are clocks inside the boxes. We know they're heavy - I just don't know if Ayane would have reacted with "I don't know sensei, this might" if she saw clocks inside. Probably not.
Regardless, maybe Akira can enter the room with the clocks during a reset, and Maya tries to prevent that, because it would bring about the end of the cycles I don't know.
If we instead assume Maya is a dream-child, then a lot changes - because she could have simply been taught how to reset the world, and a number of things that she didn't told us. Including but no limited to being the child of Akira/HOPE - but then things start to become way too crazy and without sufficient basis.

Ayane, Maya, and Sensei are trying to keep Ami from finding out about the resets, and continously do things behind her back that she can't ignore throughout Chapter 3.

For example, Ayane "borderline" kidnaps Sensei right in front of Ami while she has to work in Ayane's 'How The World Works' Chapter 3 Event:
Ami - 'What?! But I have work today! You guys aren't allowed to have fun on days that I have work!"
- "Go away, Ayane! Sensei is too busy loving me to-"

Ami - "Hey! What's the big deal?! You three show up an hour late in casual clothes and don't even ask me if I want to join in?!"
- "You guys sure talk about weird stuff when I'm not involved..."
- "Are you immortal now? Or is this just one more inside joke between you, Ayane, and Sensei that I am not a part of because you are slowly removing me from both the Love Squad and your lives?"

Tsuneyo - "Yes. She seems to be acting a bit differently as of late and I am not sure whether or not something may have happened to her."
Molly - "I...I was talking about worrying about her comedy, but...You think something happened to Ayane? She's seemed mostly the same to me."

I think there is plenty of evidence against such a clear-cut answer. Perception is one of the most recurring themes of the supernatural events. Maya says everyone sees things in different ways, and it has been shown that even if supernatural things are happening, people can see them in different ways. In the first part of the game, Yumi saves Akira from stepping into the static, and she certainly wasn't seeing any static. When he first sees Yasu, she's seeing him with someone that he isn't capable of seeing. There's an event where Kaori ignores Maya so hard it borders on her not seeing Maya at all. After her first confession, Rin starts hearing the clocks (presumably from the room with the clocks) and starts dreaming about multiple cycles, but instead of being on Akira's perspective, it's with hers and she keeps resetting until she finds a world where Chika loves her (and no one can hear or dream these things but her).

We could spend a long time listing randomly picked events where all sorts of characters see or perceive things different from how the others see them. What I mean by that is: Simply stating that because only Akira sees a specific supernatural event one way, and others see it in a different way (or at all), should not be enough to conclude that it isn't happening.

I think a more sensible answer is that we can't say for certain yet.

Going to preface this by saying that this is more of a mental exercise trying to create a basis for that possibility, and not my current take on things. If you go back to the event Scientific Research (why a beach trip between Akira, Chika, Chinami and Yumi is called that escapes me), and activate the hidden flag, Himawari will comment on how you stumbling on her there is the exact reason as to why she insisted on them having a private cafeteria.



Also, who the hell is Shiori?

On one of the early Happy Events, Am I Okay tells Akira both of them exist to fix things. And eventually HOPE and the angels start repeating the same stuff over and over, which could be interpreted as them glitching, and thus just a part of the system.


On Tick Tock Tick Tock, Am I Okay tells him that the room with the clocks is the edge of the world, instead of the end of it because Akira is stubborn. And that the point was never him learning how to escape the room with the clocks, but to climb out of his skin.



In fact, the whole Wishing Well idea is that one could have the world they wanted, and be whatever they wished to be - it feels to me like Akira's going through it thousands of times until there is a variation where he's able to break through his traumas - or at least it seems to be case in this particular cycle. There are also reference as to how he's the one able to kill god, and that one being of unlimited power (beyond the three and even NAO) will eventually show up, and they're curious as to how this being will be perceived by him.

Maybe that's USER4, which could be from Himawari to even himself, I have no idea. But that could herald the end of the resets, when he finally becomes whole, is able to take control of the cycles, "fixes" every single character through their individual routes, and reaches the true end which is the end of the simulation.

The thing being centered on Akira, despite what NAO says, is currently supported by stuff like Makoto being unable to escape during bluejay - she seems to understand the nature of what she's in as Akira tells her about the resets, and tries to follow the light by suicide (maybe like Akira did at one point by diving into the wishing well), and perhaps she couldn't because she's not the main character here, but him.

Other than that, most of the symbology also seem to gravitate around him, Nozomu is his brother, Sekai is his world, also in Tick Tock he watches as a reflection of him have sex with Am I Okay, and she tells him to make her pregnant so they can make a new HOPE and teach him to reset the world.

Himawari is general seems to believe this whole thing has to happen in order for Akira to learn something, and that he has to suffer in order to see beauty in things and lead to a happy ending (my interpretation), which is why she becomes pissed at Moyo for taking it way too far in her interview during one of the resets.

Lastly, the fact that there are users, "terminal 23", and now "template 9" seem to suggest that there is a tech part in all of this. The most concrete evidence of course would be Wires leading them in the recent update beyond the door and what the scientists/writers/workers have written in that report about how all of this is an experiment.

This could satisfy it all being real and fake at the same time. It's not like this is all a dream, the things that are happening are happening, but they're happening inside a "bubble" with real subjects that under the care of the people running the simulation.

Kind of a boring way to end up this post, but as with most things about the game, I'm not sure yet. But I definitely think there is enough to suggest that it all being more scientific than supernatural remains a possibility. Hell, maybe all of this is one big fucked up therapy session for 35 people, through the power of science, where they only leave if they're able to find a smile through tragedy and learning how to love again in a healthy manner.

What's a wishing well you're all talking about?
Click to expand...
The cycle of resets seem to happen inside of something called the Wishing Well, or could be that it's the name of that mechanic. Basically, it's a place where you can become whatever you wish and do whatever you want.

There is a recurring audio narration that states that if Akira looks down into the bottom of the well, he sees himself. It could mean that the real Akira is at the room of the clocks (at the bottom of the well), after jumping to his suicide (diving into the well). There are also some passages about him having to learn to climb out of it, while some gods tend to encourage him to simply embrace it.

Weird/Happy Ami, that appears during resets, has writings on her that say that the wishing well is a place where you wash yourself of your dreams - that can also be interpreted in the light of what I said, or something else.

Seeing as how the well seems to be central to the narrative, it's unlikely we'll receive a definitive answer much before the end.

ratmanirl said:
Wasn't it just cuz she was like secretly depressed or am I missing something here.
Click to expand...
Telling someone about the resets is a trigger for them to recover their memories. Akira tells Makoto about them and that's when she gets the idea to jump. If not for that, she'd have probably just kissed him. But the game was rigged from the start, because even before all that Akira says he's feeling callous that night.

Yasu says to Akira that his mother hated when he was consumed by the dark, since she believed in the light. HOPE is associated with a blinding light. Planting seeds of corruption is a common theme with Sekai. Also, Akira is kind of a dick during the whole conversation.



Then, there are a references to multiple cycles, them being in a prison and the light of the moon (these all have multiple meanings)



Makoto goes to say she gives up on being without guidance. Then she says she wants to become a bird (HOPE is the thing with feathers), and that idea just "came" to her as a means to escape the darkness towards the light of the moon again. She also mentions a shadow that's been looming over her. By that point, Akira begins to question if that is even Makoto.




We arrive at the most important moment, Akira describes the cycle of resets. In this version he says that he turned to god (in this case HOPE, to whom he turned during the first reset). Then Makoto asks him to close his eyes because you can see more with your eyes closed, which is something people that follow HOPE say all the time. Remember Yasu covering her eyes for that whole ceremony at the church.



She had the idea to become a bluejay walking over there as she said she couldn't go on without guidance, but she truly SAW the light when he talked about the resets and requesting HOPE's help. As Yasu points out all the time, HOPE's sphere is light. That part about him doing so much for her might be her getting an insight on the nature of the Wishing Well and Akira's part in fixing them, but there's not enough to support that.



We jump to the Main Event Happy Places, in which Makoto talks to Akira with her eyes all fucked up after jumping, being brought back, and retaining her memories. What she's saying here is most likely pointing to the inescapable reality of the cycles, since, even if one would not follow into the supernatural theory, she died and was put back.



Makoto explains that this was not due to Akira's corruption at all, she remembers jumping, and she knows that she was broken (by HOPE most likely). Am I Okay says previously not to trust HOPE and how it's all a trap. Then she struggles with what was done to her after she gave herself to him - she's not talking about being brought back obviously, that would be a good thing. She's talking about being consumed (and probably violated by the dark).

This part is a bit confusing to me because HOPE is supposed to be the light, and his previous state (Nozomu) was all about using everyone as a cock-sleeve - so I don't get the mention of the dark here, as the light is already fucked up enough, also as what we see with Yasu shows. Nevertheless, Makoto was betrayed.



Further pointing out things were done to her. And when she says that nothing is real, that sentence is completed in Akira's head. Could be completed by him, or someone else. But it plays as a revelation shared between him and Makoto, now that she's been with the dark.


Final thoughts: I don't remember what she says about all this, or if HOPE mentions her in the future, haven't made it there in my replay, but going off of this, she seemed to have given herself to HOPE and got a really bad deal out of it. Dude didn't even had the decency to erase her memories when he put her back.

I can't reallly pinpoint just how much insight she gained throughout the scene, or after the incident until the second reset. She was definitely depressed, but I find it very hard to believe that she would ask Akira to be a witness to her suicide out of the blue, in a world where her father still lived.

posts.content_html_raw:
Akira reflects on his nature, his job to fix people and its relation to the Wishing Well.
What's next is Akira's reflection on the nature of puzzles and his part in it.

He mentions sixteen puzzles and those are likely the sixteen students in his class (we're at the beginning of chapter 2). His transformation always being incomplete may be a reference to how Am I Okay says that while he's changing more than before, he still hasn't learned to climb out of his skin.



Him trying to brute force his way into fixing the girls' problems and how they all break but him, cause they just get reset.



Now comes the most interesting part. It has been hinted a few times about Akira's possibility of also becoming a god. But it also is a callback to what Am I Okay says about being his job to fix things, and that the edge of the world never becomes the end of it because he's stubborn.

So what if Akira is trying to fix every girl through this prison/simulation/dream/something called the Wishing Well? That's the ultimate puzzle, they're all waiting to be fixed at the same time while getting tangled with the others. If he manages to solve it, he becomes God.

But maybe that's a thing he's also reluctant about? Maybe he fears that he will have to fix himself too and that's scary, or maybe he's scared that if he finishes his job then the Well will come to an end and he'll finally hit the ground? (maybe he's still falling, between having jumped and dying, and what awaits at the end is the sidewalk).


I wasn't expecting this out of a random Kirin event, but I thought it was interesting enough to share it.

I think this is a rather interesting topic. Because I feel like it's more of a "problem" (or maybe simply the intent) with the way the story is written. Futaba is just not a compelling character, as it has been pointed out by many people here, as well as herself and Akira. For instance, Io shares some traits with Futaba in her extreme lack of self-worth, yet Io is highly compelling.

Yumi bullies Futaba many times over, but that's just in the beginning which is then followed by "The Town has Two Halves" which radically changes our perception of her forever. I don't think it would be a stretch to say that we all feel some sort of collective guilt or pity for what has been done to her.

Then what happens? Yumi steadily grows, shows her affection for Akira at increasing rates, has a compelling emotional turmoil about liking a person that forced himself on her, has to endure being cucked by Chika constantly, either by being present or having to take care of Chinami for her best friend to have sex with the man she likes, gets in touch with her mom, gets a job, gets into the apocalypse squad, and not to count saving Akira so many times.

What about Futaba? (...) Her parents are architects and she writes an interesting horror story. Other than that, there's the stuff about Nodoka writing her book, but we already had Ayane's list of people that Akira was sleeping with, and her being assaulted by Kirin, which both served a similar purpose, way before this and were way more compelling too. Futaba just always feels to me like too little and too late. She could have known about what Nodoka did "in her name" and had something interesting happen out of that, but we were denied that too.

In fact there's so little about her that being bullied by Yumi is one of her defining traits and that hasn't happened since chapter 1.

Moonflare said:
I think this is a rather interesting topic. Because I feel like it's more of a "problem" (or maybe simply the intent) with the way the story is written. Futaba is just not a compelling character, as it has been pointed out by many people here, as well as herself and Akira. For instance, Io shares some traits with Futaba in her extreme lack of self-worth, yet Io is highly compelling.

Yumi bullies Futaba many times over, but that's just in the beginning which is then followed by "The Town has Two Halves" which radically changes our perception of her forever. I don't think it would be a stretch to say that we all feel some sort of collective guilt or pity for what has been done to her.

Then what happens? Yumi steadily grows, shows her affection for Akira at increasing rates, has a compelling emotional turmoil about liking a person that forced himself on her, has to endure being cucked by Chika constantly, either by being present or having to take care of Chinami for her best friend to have sex with the man she likes, gets in touch with her mom, gets a job, gets into the apocalypse squad, and not to count saving Akira so many times.

What about Futaba? (...) Her parents are architects and she writes an interesting horror story. Other than that, there's the stuff about Nodoka writing her book, but we already had Ayane's list of people that Akira was sleeping with, and her being assaulted by Kirin, which both served a similar purpose, way before this and were way more compelling too. Futaba just always feels to me like too little and too late. She could have known about what Nodoka did "in her name" and had something interesting happen out of that, but we were denied that too.

In fact there's so little about her that being bullied by Yumi is one of her defining traits and that hasn't happened since chapter 1.
Click to expand...
Yumi didn't actually stop bullying Futaba until Chapter 3, though.

Yumi just couldn't do much to Futaba after Chapter 1, except for that one time, with Sensei around, where she forced Futaba against a wall and threatened to kill her in Chapter 2:
Yumi - "I should fucking kill you right here!"

Nevertheless, Futaba's still traumatized by Yumi, and she seems to be her main source of trauma. Seeing Yuki caused her to have a panic attack (and Yuki to apologize for Yumi), and Yumi is likely why Futaba reacted the way she did about the book:

- "They're going to hurt me..."

Futaba couldn't bathe, sit, or even read with Yumi around, who was trying to steal her towel, mock her body, or steal her desk, whenever. Of course, there's also how Yumi fueled Futaba's bulimia and helped scar her insides.

That shit wouldn't fly after Chapter 1, though:
Nodoka - "But that doesn't change the fact that I am tired of this girl thinking she's allowed to just hurt you whenever her withered heart desires."
Nodoka wouldn't let Yumi around her. Tsuneyo was also there for more than enough muscle. Then there's also Ayane, who's defended Futaba, and embarassed Yumi before.

As for Futaba, she didn't get mouthraped or...spent like 3 chapters looking for a job, before crawling back to the mother who ditched her, like Yumi, but Futaba:

Especially now that Pareidolia finally assumed a great idea of control and revealed its true nature to Sensei already, why does it need to keep lying? If there was an elusive reason or goal for it to keep lying, it'd have to be something that cannot be achieved by continuing toying Sensei, and can only be achieved by Sensei actively choosing it; this reason or goal was never articulated anywhere, and I am not about putting my faith in future evidence when there isn't one. Getting its own season doesn't quite count because that's a mean to an end and not an end (getting its own season so that it can do things vs just getting its own season).

And the reason I brought up Sensei's exchange with Pareidolia again is because, Sensei is proven to be an absolute dunce when trying to figure out who did what. I admit I don't know how much Sensei can see what we see and it's hard to prove anything, but that's not my point. The point is we saw an USER2 on the screen during Molly incident, but when Sensei tried to wrap his head around about it, he first thought it was Pareidolia because this is a nostalgic trick he experienced, and then he thought it was HOPE because I assume Sensei was associating this trick with the one that said "take something that doesn't belong to you", and Pareidolia had to "correct" him that it was USER2 that did it. I almost don't need to care whether Sensei could see what we see or not because he just got it all wrong; Pareidolia's supposed plan to pin blame on USER2 never worked as intended because Sensei was too dumb to point at the right scapegoat anyway. This is another reason why I would have to regard Pareidolia's statement on Molly incident as true because, Sensei was too much of a dunce to get properly deceived on the matter. Since I believe "Pareidolia trying to gain trust" is true, then "Pareidolia being powerful enough and being responsible for Molly incident" would have to be false.

Yours:
Pareidolia claimed Molly incident was caused by USER2 but the entire exchange was very back-and-forth → Pareidolia cannot be trusted due to preconceived solid reasons → This means that statement he gave has a good chance to be false → Molly incident might not be caused by USER2 → Bear in mind that Pareidolia communicated in USER2 fashion twice → This might imply the possibility of Pareidolia impersonating USER2 at some other occasions before Chapter 4 → USER2 never outright admitted that was his doing → Pareidolia could actually be the culprit behind Molly incident and was trying to pin blame on USER2 (or the possibility was there I should say) → All the more reasons to believe as such because Pareidolia was such a lying fuck since the beginning (it is)

Mine:
Pareidolia claimed Molly incident was caused by USER2 but the entire exchange was very back-and-forth → Pareidolia cannot be trusted due to preconceived solid reasons → Its days of gaining Sensei's trust are over, however → I don't find a reason for Pareidolia to still lie to Sensei about it at this point → Molly incident might just be caused by USER2 → USER2 never said it was him but this topic never came up between Sensei and USER2 so at best it's unconfirmed → Pareidolia's statement at least aligns with what we saw on screen during Molly incident → Are there direct evidences that can prove Molly incident was done by someone other than USER2? → Currently no → USER2 was for now the one responsible for Molly incident, and Pareidolia was trying to replicate a "successful" case by pulling the same trick on Karin

My weakness here is that I don't find an in-game reason for Pareidolia to keep lying about something Sensei could never figure out on his own, and I don't find other direct evidence which can prove that USER2 didn't do it. So feel free to give me pointers. And definitely correct me if I got your part wrong.

absolute dunce
when trying to figure out who did what. I admit I don't know how much Sensei can see what we see and it's hard to prove anything, but that's not my point. The point is we saw an
USER2
on the screen during Molly incident, but when Sensei tried to wrap his head around about it, he first thought it was
Pareidolia
because this is a nostalgic trick he experienced, and then he thought it was
HOPE
because I assume Sensei was associating this trick with the one that said "take something that doesn't belong to you", and Pareidolia had to "correct" him that it was
USER2
that did it. I almost don't need to care whether Sensei could see what we see or not because
he just got it
all wrong
; Pareidolia's supposed plan to pin blame on USER2 never worked as intended because Sensei was too dumb to point at the right scapegoat anyway.

Since I believe "Pareidolia trying to gain trust" is true, then "Pareidolia being powerful enough and being responsible for Molly incident" would have to be false.

Pareidolia claimed Molly incident was caused by USER2 but the entire exchange was very back-and-forth
→
Pareidolia cannot be trusted due to preconceived solid reasons
→
This means that statement he gave has a good chance to be false

Molly incident might not be caused by USER2
